verses.1:1: Paul, an apostle of Christ Jesus through the will of God, and our brother Timothy, to the church of God that is in Corinth, together with all the saints who are throughout all Achaia:
verses.1:2: Grace be to you and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
verses.1:3: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of compassions and the God of all consolation,
verses.1:4: who consoles us in all our affliction, so that we may be able to console those who are in any affliction through the consolation with which we ourselves are consoled by God.
verses.1:5: For just as the sufferings of Christ abound to us, so through Christ our consolation also abounds.
verses.1:6: Now if we are afflicted, it is for your consolation and salvation; and if we are consoled, it is for your consolation, which works effectively in the patient endurance of the same sufferings that we also suffer;
verses.1:7: and our hope for you is steadfast, knowing that as you are partakers of the sufferings, so also you are of the consolation.
verses.1:8: For we do not want you to be unaware, brethren, concerning the affliction that befell us in Asia: we were weighed down beyond measure, beyond our strength, so that we despaired even of life.
verses.1:9: Indeed, we ourselves had the sentence of death within us, so that we should not rely on ourselves, but on God who raises the dead,
verses.1:10: who delivered us from so great a death, and will deliver us; in Him we have set our hope that He will deliver us yet again,
verses.1:11: as you also join in helping us by supplication on our behalf, so that thanks may be given by many on our behalf for the gracious gift granted to us through many persons.
verses.1:12: For our boasting is this, the testimony of our conscience: that we conducted ourselves in the world in holiness and sincerity from God, not in fleshly wisdom but in the grace of God, and even more abundantly toward you.
verses.1:13: For we write nothing else to you than what you read or also understand; and I hope that you will understand to the full,
verses.1:14: just as you have also understood us in part, that we are your boast, even as you also are ours, in the day of our Lord Jesus.
verses.1:15: And with this confidence I intended to come to you first, so that you might receive a second favor,
verses.1:16: and to pass by way of you into Macedonia, and from Macedonia to return to you again, and to be sent on my way by you to Judea.
verses.1:17: Therefore, when I was intending this, did I act with fickleness? Or do I form my plans according to the flesh, so that with me there should be "Yes, yes" and "No, no"?
verses.1:18: But as God is faithful, our word to you is not "Yes" and "No."
verses.1:19: For the Son of God, Jesus Christ, who was proclaimed among you by us—by me and Silvanus and Timothy—was not "Yes" and "No," but in Him it has been "Yes."
verses.1:20: For however many promises of God there are, in Him is the "Yes"; therefore also through Him is the "Amen" to God, for glory through us.
verses.1:21: Now He who establishes us together with you in Christ, and anointed us, is God,
verses.1:22: who also set His seal upon us and gave us the pledge of the Spirit in our hearts.
verses.1:23: Moreover, I call upon God as witness against my own soul that it was to spare you that I did not come again to Corinth.
verses.1:24: Not that we exercise lordship over your faith, but we are fellow workers for your joy; for by faith you stand firm.
verses.2:1: For I resolved this for myself, not to come to you once more in sorrow.
verses.2:2: For if I cause you sorrow, then who is there to make me glad, except the very one who is made sorrowful by me?
verses.2:3: And I wrote this very thing lest, upon coming, I should suffer sorrow from those over whom I ought to rejoice; for I am confident in all of you that my joy belongs to all of you.
verses.2:4: For out of much affliction and anguish of heart I wrote to you with many tears, not so that you might be grieved, but so that you might know the love that I bear so abundantly for you.
verses.2:5: Now if anyone has caused sorrow, he has not caused sorrow to me, but in part—lest I be too severe—to all of you.
verses.2:6: For such a man, this punishment by the majority is sufficient,
verses.2:7: so that, on the contrary, you should rather forgive and console him, lest somehow such a one be swallowed up by excessive sorrow.
verses.2:8: Therefore I exhort you to confirm your love for him.
verses.2:9: For it was also for this purpose that I wrote, so that I might know your proven character, whether you are obedient in everything.
verses.2:10: And to whomever you forgive anything, I forgive also; for indeed, what I have forgiven—if I have forgiven anything—I have done for your sake in the presence of Christ,
verses.2:11: so that Satan may not gain an advantage over us, for we are not unaware of his designs.
verses.2:12: Now when I arrived at Troas for the gospel of Christ, and a door stood open for me in the Lord,
verses.2:13: I had no rest in my spirit because I did not find my brother Titus; so taking leave of them, I departed for Macedonia.
verses.2:14: But thanks be to God, who always leads us in triumphal procession in Christ, and makes manifest through us the fragrance of the knowledge of Him in every place.
verses.2:15: For we are the sweet aroma of Christ to God among those who are being saved and among those who are perishing:
verses.2:16: to the one, a fragrance from death to death; to the other, a fragrance from life to life. And who is sufficient for such things?
verses.2:17: For we are not like the many, peddling the word of God; rather, as from sincerity, as from God, we speak before God in Christ.
verses.3:1: Are we beginning to commend ourselves again? Or do we need, as some do, letters of commendation to you or from you?
verses.3:2: You yourselves are our letter, inscribed upon our hearts, known and read by all men,
verses.3:3: plainly shown to be a letter of Christ, ministered by us, inscribed not with ink but with the Spirit of the living God, not on tablets of stone but on tablets that are hearts of flesh.
verses.3:4: Now such is the confidence that we have through Christ toward God.
verses.3:5: Not that we are sufficient in ourselves to account anything as coming from ourselves; rather, our sufficiency comes from God,
verses.3:6: who also made us sufficient to be ministers of a new covenant, not of the letter but of the Spirit; for the letter puts to death, while the Spirit makes alive.
verses.3:7: Now if the ministry of death, engraved in letters upon stones, came with glory, so that the sons of Israel could not gaze intently upon the face of Moses because of the glory of his countenance, a glory that was passing away,
verses.3:8: how shall the ministry of the Spirit not be even more in glory?
verses.3:9: For if the ministry of condemnation had glory, much more does the ministry of righteousness abound in glory.
verses.3:10: For indeed, what had been glorified has come to have no glory in this respect, on account of the surpassing glory.
verses.3:11: For if that which is passing away came through glory, much more does that which abides remain in glory.
verses.3:12: Therefore, having such a hope, we exercise great boldness,
verses.3:13: and are not like Moses, who would place a veil over his face so that the sons of Israel might not gaze steadily at the end of what was passing away.
verses.3:14: But their minds were hardened; for until this very day the same veil remains unlifted at the reading of the old covenant, because in Christ it is done away with.
verses.3:15: Indeed, even to this day, whenever Moses is read, a veil lies over their heart;
verses.3:16: yet whenever one turns to the Lord, the veil is taken away.
verses.3:17: And the Lord is the Spirit, and wherever the Spirit of the Lord is, there is liberty.
verses.3:18: And all of us, with unveiled face, beholding the glory of the Lord as in a mirror, are being transformed into the very same image from glory to glory, even as from the Lord, who is the Spirit.
verses.4:1: Therefore, having this ministry just as we have been shown mercy, we do not lose heart;
verses.4:2: rather, we have renounced the secret things of shame, neither walking in cunning nor adulterating the word of God, but by the open manifestation of the truth commending ourselves to every human conscience in the presence of God.
verses.4:3: Yet even if our gospel is veiled, it is veiled among those who are perishing,
verses.4:4: in whose case the god of this age has blinded the minds of the unbelieving, lest the radiant light of the gospel of the glory of Christ, who is the image of God, should shine forth.
verses.4:5: For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Christ Jesus as Lord, and ourselves as your servants for the sake of Jesus.
verses.4:6: For God, who spoke, "Out of darkness light shall shine," is the One who has shone in our hearts to bring the illumination of the knowledge of the glory of God in the face of Jesus Christ.
verses.4:7: Yet we hold this treasure in vessels of clay, so that the surpassing greatness of the power may belong to God and not come from us;
verses.4:8: pressed hard in every way, yet not crushed; perplexed, yet not driven to despair;
verses.4:9: persecuted, yet not abandoned; thrown down, yet not destroyed,
verses.4:10: continually bearing about in the body the dying of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be made manifest in our body.
verses.4:11: For we who are living are continually given over to death for the sake of Jesus, so that the life of Jesus may also be made manifest in our mortal flesh.
verses.4:12: Thus death is at work in us, yet life in you.
verses.4:13: Yet having the same spirit of faith, in accordance with what stands written, "I believed; therefore I spoke," we also believe, and therefore we also speak,
verses.4:14: knowing that He who raised Jesus will also raise us with Jesus and present us together with you.
verses.4:15: For all things are on your behalf, so that grace, increasing through the greater number, may make thanksgiving overflow to the glory of God.
verses.4:16: For this reason we do not lose heart; rather, even though our outer man is wasting away, our inner man is renewed day after day.
verses.4:17: For this momentary lightness of our affliction is working out for us, in measure beyond all measure, an eternal weight of glory,
verses.4:18: as we fix our gaze not on the things that are seen, but on the things that are unseen; for the things that are seen are transient, but the things that are unseen are eternal.
verses.5:1: For we know that if our earthly tent-dwelling is torn down, we have a building from God, a house not fashioned by hands, eternal in the heavens.
verses.5:2: Indeed, in this we groan, yearning deeply to be clothed over with our dwelling from heaven,
verses.5:3: if indeed, once clothed, we shall not be found naked.
verses.5:4: For while we remain in this tent, we groan under our burden, because we do not wish to be unclothed, but rather to be clothed over, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
verses.5:5: Now the One who has prepared us for this very purpose is God, who has given to us the pledge of the Spirit.
verses.5:6: Therefore we are always of good courage, knowing that while we are at home in the body, we are away from the Lord—
verses.5:7: for by faith we walk, and not by sight—
verses.5:8: we are of good courage, indeed, and are well pleased rather to be away from the body and to make our home with the Lord.
verses.5:9: Therefore we also make it our ambition, whether at home or away, to be pleasing to Him.
verses.5:10: For all of us must appear openly before the judgment seat of Christ, so that each one may receive what is due for the deeds done through the body, according to what he has done, whether good or evil.
verses.5:11: Knowing therefore the fear of the Lord, we persuade men; yet to God we are clearly known, and I trust that we are clearly known in your consciences as well.
verses.5:12: We are not commending ourselves to you once again, but rather giving you an occasion to boast on our behalf, so that you may have a reply for those who boast in outward appearance and not in the heart.
verses.5:13: For if we are beside ourselves, it is for God; if we are in our right mind, it is for your sake.
verses.5:14: For the love of Christ constrains us, since we have reached this conviction: that One died on behalf of all, and therefore all have died;
verses.5:15: and He died on behalf of all, so that those who live should no longer live for themselves, but for Him who died for their sake and was raised.
verses.5:16: Consequently, from now on we know no one according to the flesh; even if we once knew Christ according to the flesh, yet now we know Him in that way no longer.
verses.5:17: Therefore, if anyone is in Christ, there is a new creation; the old things have passed away; behold, new things have come into being.
verses.5:18: Now all these things are from God, who reconciled us to Himself through Christ and gave to us the ministry of reconciliation,
verses.5:19: namely, that God was in Christ reconciling the world to Himself, not reckoning their trespasses against them, and entrusting to us the word of reconciliation.
verses.5:20: Therefore we serve as ambassadors on behalf of Christ, as though God were making His appeal through us; we implore you for the sake of Christ: be reconciled to God.
verses.5:21: The One who knew no sin, He made to be sin on our behalf, so that in Him we might become the righteousness of God.
verses.6:1: Working together with Him, we also urge you not to receive the grace of God in vain;
verses.6:2: for He says, "At a favorable time I listened to you, and on a day of salvation I came to your aid." Behold, now is the most favorable time; behold, now is the day of salvation.
verses.6:3: We put no cause of stumbling in anything, so that the ministry may not be discredited,
verses.6:4: rather, in everything we commend ourselves as servants of God: in great endurance, in afflictions, in hardships, in distresses,
verses.6:5: in beatings, in imprisonments, in tumults, in toils, in sleepless nights, in fastings;
verses.6:6: in purity, in knowledge, in forbearance, in kindness, in the Holy Spirit, in unfeigned love,
verses.6:7: in the word of truth, in the power of God; with the weapons of righteousness for the right hand and the left,
verses.6:8: through honor and dishonor, through ill report and good report; as impostors, yet truthful;
verses.6:9: as unknown, yet well known; as dying, and behold, we live; as disciplined, yet not put to death;
verses.6:10: as grieving, yet always rejoicing; as impoverished, yet enriching many; as having nothing, yet possessing all things.
verses.6:11: Our mouth stands open to you, Corinthians; our heart has been opened wide.
verses.6:12: You are not restricted in us; rather, you are restricted in your own affections.
verses.6:13: Now in equal return—I speak as to children—open wide your hearts also.
verses.6:14: Do not become unequally yoked with unbelievers. For what partnership is there between righteousness and lawlessness, or what fellowship does light have with darkness?
verses.6:15: And what harmony is there between Christ and Beliar, or what portion does a believer share with an unbeliever?
verses.6:16: And what agreement does the temple of God have with idols? For we are the temple of the living God, just as God has said: "I will dwell among them and walk among them; I will be their God, and they shall be My people."
verses.6:17: Therefore, "Come out from their midst and be separated," says the Lord, "and do not touch anything unclean; and I will welcome you,
verses.6:18: and I will be a Father to you, and you shall be sons and daughters to Me," says the Lord Almighty.
verses.7:1: Therefore, having these promises, beloved, let us purify ourselves from every defilement of flesh and spirit, bringing holiness to perfection in the fear of God.
verses.7:2: Make room for us; we have wronged no one, we have ruined no one, we have defrauded no one.
verses.7:3: I do not speak by way of condemnation, for I have already said that you are in our hearts, to die together and to live together.
verses.7:4: Great is my candor toward you, great is my boasting concerning you; I am filled with comfort; I overflow exceedingly with joy in all our affliction.
verses.7:5: For indeed, when we came into Macedonia, our flesh had no relief, but we were afflicted in every way—conflicts outside, fears within—
verses.7:6: yet God, who comforts those who are cast down, comforted us through the arrival of Titus;
verses.7:7: and not only by his arrival, but also by the comfort with which he was comforted over you, while he reported to us your deep longing, your mourning, and your zeal on my behalf, so that I rejoiced all the more.
verses.7:8: For even if I caused you sorrow by the letter, I do not regret it; even though I did regret it (I see that that letter caused you sorrow, though only for a while),
verses.7:9: now I rejoice, not because you were made sorrowful, but because you were made sorrowful to repentance; for you were made sorrowful according to God, so that in nothing you might suffer loss from us.
verses.7:10: For sorrow according to God works repentance to salvation without regret, whereas the sorrow of the world produces death.
verses.7:11: For behold this very thing, that you were made sorrowful according to God: what great earnestness it produced in you—indeed, what defense, what indignation, what fear, what longing, what zeal, what avenging of wrong! In every respect you have demonstrated yourselves to be innocent in the matter.
verses.7:12: Therefore, although I wrote to you, it was not for the sake of the one who did the wrong, nor for the sake of the one who was wronged, but in order that your earnestness on our behalf might be made manifest to you in the sight of God.
verses.7:13: For this reason we have been comforted. And besides our comfort, we rejoiced all the more exceedingly over the joy of Titus, because his spirit has been refreshed by all of you;
verses.7:14: for if in anything I have boasted to him about you, I was not put to shame; rather, just as we spoke all things to you in truth, so also our boasting before Titus has proved to be truth.
verses.7:15: And his tender affection for you abounds all the more as he calls to mind the obedience of all of you, how you welcomed him with fear and trembling.
verses.7:16: I rejoice because in every respect I have confidence in you.
verses.8:1: Now we make known to you, brethren, the grace of God which has been given among the churches of Macedonia,
verses.8:2: that in a great testing of affliction, the abundance of their joy and their profound poverty abounded into the wealth of their generosity;
verses.8:3: for I bear witness that they gave according to their ability, yes, and beyond their ability, of their own free will,
verses.8:4: imploring us with much urgency for the grace and the fellowship of the ministry to the saints—
verses.8:5: and not as we had hoped, but they gave themselves first to the Lord, and to us through the will of God,
verses.8:6: so that we urged Titus that, just as he had previously begun, so he would also complete among you this grace as well;
verses.8:7: yet just as you abound in every respect—in faith and speech and knowledge and all earnestness, and in the love from us that is in you—see that you abound in this grace as well.
verses.8:8: I do not speak by way of command, yet through the earnestness of others I am testing the genuineness of your love as well;
verses.8:9: for you know the grace of our Lord Jesus Christ, that on your account He became poor, though being rich, in order that through His poverty you might be rich.
verses.8:10: And in this matter I give my judgment, for this is to your benefit, you who since last year began not only to do it, but also to desire it;
verses.8:11: but now finish the doing of it as well, so that just as there was eagerness in willing, so also there may be completion from what you possess.
verses.8:12: For if the eagerness is present, it is well received according to whatever a person has, not according to what he does not have.
verses.8:13: For it is not that there should be relief for others and affliction for you, but by way of equality:
verses.8:14: at the present time your abundance is for their want, so that their abundance may also come to meet your want, in order that there may be equality;
verses.8:15: just as it is written: "He who had much did not have an excess, and he who had little did not fall short."
verses.8:16: Now thanks be to God, who places the same earnestness for you in the heart of Titus,
verses.8:17: because he indeed welcomed our appeal, yet being even more earnest, he set out to you of his own free will.
verses.8:18: And together with him we have sent the brother whose praise in the gospel goes through all the churches—
verses.8:19: and not only that, but he has also been appointed by the churches as our fellow traveler with this grace that is being administered by us for the glory of the Lord Himself and our own eagerness—
verses.8:20: guarding against this, lest anyone find fault with us concerning this bountiful offering which is being administered by us,
verses.8:21: for we take thought for what is honorable not only before the Lord, but also before men.
verses.8:22: And together with them we have sent our brother, whom we have tested many times in many matters and found earnest, yet now far more earnest because of great confidence in you.
verses.8:23: As for Titus, he is my partner and fellow laborer on your behalf; as for our brethren, they are envoys of the churches, the glory of Christ.
verses.8:24: Therefore, manifest to them, before the face of the churches, the proof of your love and of our boasting concerning you.
verses.9:1: For indeed, concerning the ministry for the saints, it is unnecessary for me to write to you,
verses.9:2: for I know your readiness, concerning which I boast on your behalf to the Macedonians, that Achaia has been prepared since last year; and your zeal has roused the majority of them.
verses.9:3: Yet I have sent the brethren, lest our boast concerning you prove empty in this particular, so that, just as I was saying, you may be prepared,
verses.9:4: lest somehow, if Macedonians come with me and find you unprepared, we—not to say you—should be put to shame in this confidence.
verses.9:5: Therefore I considered it necessary to urge the brethren to go on ahead to you and arrange in advance your previously promised blessing, so that it may be ready in this way as a blessing and not as covetousness.
verses.9:6: Now know this: he who sows sparingly shall also reap sparingly, and he who sows with blessings shall also reap with blessings.
verses.9:7: Let each one give just as he has resolved in his heart, not out of sorrow or under compulsion; for God loves a joyful giver.
verses.9:8: And God has power to make every grace abound to you, so that in every respect, at all times, having all sufficiency, you may abound toward every good work;
verses.9:9: (just as it is written: "He has scattered abroad, he has given to the poor; his righteousness abides forever";
verses.9:10: now He who provides seed to the sower and bread for food shall supply and multiply your seed, and shall increase the produce of your righteousness);
verses.9:11: being enriched in every respect for all generosity, which through us brings about thanksgiving to God—
verses.9:12: for the ministry of this sacred service is not only fully supplying the wants of the saints, but is also overflowing through many thanksgivings to God—
verses.9:13: by the proof afforded by this ministry, they glorify God for the submission of your confession to the gospel of Christ, and for the generosity of your fellowship toward them and toward all,
verses.9:14: and in their supplication on your behalf, yearning for you because of the surpassing grace of God upon you.
verses.9:15: Thanks be to God for His gift beyond all telling!
verses.10:1: Now I myself, Paul, appeal to you by the meekness and gentleness of Christ—I who when face to face am lowly among you, yet when absent am bold toward you;
verses.10:2: and I implore you that when I am present I may not have to be bold with that confidence by which I intend to be daring against some who regard us as walking according to the flesh.
verses.10:3: For although we walk in the flesh, we do not conduct our warfare according to the flesh—
verses.10:4: for the weapons of our warfare are not of the flesh, but mighty before God for the tearing down of strongholds—tearing down reasonings
verses.10:5: and every lofty height that raises itself against the knowledge of God, and leading every thought captive into the obedience of Christ,
verses.10:6: and holding ourselves ready to punish every act of disobedience, whenever your obedience is made complete.
verses.10:7: Look at what is before your face. If anyone is convinced in himself that he belongs to Christ, let him consider this again within himself, that just as he belongs to Christ, so also do we.
verses.10:8: For even if I boast somewhat more regarding our authority, which the Lord gave for building you up and not for tearing you down, I shall not be put to shame,
verses.10:9: lest I should appear as if I sought to terrify you through my letters;
verses.10:10: for "His letters," one says, "are weighty and mighty, yet his bodily presence is weak, and his speech is despised."
verses.10:11: Let such a person consider this: that just as we are in word through letters when absent, such shall we also be in deed when present.
verses.10:12: For we do not dare to rank or compare ourselves with certain ones who commend themselves; rather, measuring themselves by themselves and comparing themselves with themselves, they are without understanding.
verses.10:13: We, however, shall not boast beyond measure, but according to the measure of the domain that God apportioned to us as a measure, to reach even as far as you—
verses.10:14: for we are not overextending ourselves as though we did not reach to you, since we came all the way even to you with the gospel of Christ—
verses.10:15: not boasting beyond measure in the labors of others, yet having hope that, as your faith grows, we shall be greatly enlarged among you according to our domain to overflowing,
verses.10:16: so as to preach the gospel in the regions beyond you, and not to boast in another's domain concerning work already prepared.
verses.10:17: Yet let him who boasts, boast in the Lord;
verses.10:18: for it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends.
verses.11:1: Oh, that you would bear with me in a little foolishness—yet indeed, do bear with me!
verses.11:2: For I am jealous for you with a godly jealousy, because I betrothed you to one husband, to present you as a pure virgin to Christ;
verses.11:3: yet I fear lest somehow, just as the serpent deceived Eve by his craftiness, your minds should be corrupted from the sincerity and purity that are toward Christ.
verses.11:4: For if indeed the one who comes preaches another Jesus whom we did not preach, or if you receive a different spirit which you did not receive, or a different gospel which you did not accept, you bear with it readily enough!
verses.11:5: For I consider that I am in no way inferior to these superlative apostles.
verses.11:6: And even if I am unskilled in speech, yet I am not so in knowledge; rather, in every way we have made this manifest to you in all things.
verses.11:7: Or did I commit a sin by humbling myself so that you might be exalted, because I preached the gospel of God to you without charge?
verses.11:8: I plundered other churches, taking wages from them for my ministry to you,
verses.11:9: and when I was present with you and fell into need, I was a burden to no one; for what I lacked, the brethren who came from Macedonia fully supplied. And in everything I kept myself from being burdensome to you, and so I shall keep myself.
verses.11:10: As the truth of Christ is in me, this boasting of mine shall not be silenced in the regions of Achaia.
verses.11:11: Why? Because I do not love you? God knows.
verses.11:12: Yet what I am doing I shall also continue to do, so that I may cut off the opportunity of those who desire an opportunity, that in the matter of which they boast they may be found to be just as we are.
verses.11:13: For such men are false apostles, treacherous workmen, disguising themselves as apostles of Christ;
verses.11:14: and it is no marvel, for Satan himself disguises himself as an angel of light;
verses.11:15: therefore it is no great thing if his ministers also disguise themselves as ministers of righteousness, whose end shall be according to their works.
verses.11:16: Again I say, let no one suppose me to be a fool—yet if otherwise, receive me even as a fool, so that I also may boast a little.
verses.11:17: What I speak, I do not speak according to the Lord, but as it were in foolishness, in this assurance of boasting.
verses.11:18: Since many boast according to the flesh, I also shall boast.
verses.11:19: For you gladly bear with fools, being so wise yourselves!
verses.11:20: For you bear with it if someone brings you into bondage, if someone devours you, if someone takes advantage of you, if someone exalts himself, if someone strikes you in the face.
verses.11:21: To my shame I say it, as though we have been too weak! Yet in whatever anyone dares to boast—I speak in foolishness—I dare also.
verses.11:22: Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they the seed of Abraham? So am I.
verses.11:23: Are they ministers of Christ? I speak as one out of his mind—I am more so: in labors far more abundantly, in imprisonments far more often, in beatings beyond measure, in deaths many times;
verses.11:24: from the Jews five times I received forty lashes less one;
verses.11:25: three times I was beaten with rods, once I was stoned, three times I suffered shipwreck, a night and a day I have spent in the deep;
verses.11:26: on frequent journeys, in perils of rivers, in perils of robbers, in perils from my own people, in perils from the Gentiles, in perils in the city, in perils in the wilderness, in perils on the sea, in perils among false brethren,
verses.11:27: in labor and hardship, in sleeplessness often, in hunger and thirst, in fastings often, in cold and nakedness.
verses.11:28: Apart from the other things, there is the daily pressure upon me: my anxious care for all the churches.
verses.11:29: Who is weak, and I am not weak? Who is made to stumble, and I do not burn?
verses.11:30: If I must boast, I shall boast of the things concerning my weakness.
verses.11:31: The God and Father of the Lord Jesus, who is blessed forever, knows that I do not lie.
verses.11:32: In Damascus the governor under King Aretas was guarding the city of the Damascenes in order to seize me,
verses.11:33: and I was lowered in a woven basket through a window in the wall, and escaped from his hands.
verses.12:1: Boasting is necessary; though indeed it is not profitable, yet I shall move on to visions and revelations of the Lord.
verses.12:2: I know a man in Christ who fourteen years ago—whether in the body I do not know, or outside the body I do not know, God knows—such a man was caught up as far as the third heaven.
verses.12:3: And I know such a man—whether in the body or apart from the body I do not know, God knows—
verses.12:4: that he was snatched up into Paradise and heard unutterable sayings, which no man is permitted to speak.
verses.12:5: On behalf of such a man I shall boast, yet on behalf of myself I shall not boast, except in weaknesses.
verses.12:6: For even if I should desire to boast, I shall not be a fool, because I shall speak the truth; yet I refrain, lest anyone should credit to me more than what he sees in me or hears from me,
verses.12:7: even by reason of the surpassing greatness of the revelations. Therefore, lest I should exalt myself beyond measure, a thorn in the flesh was given to me, a messenger of Satan, to batter me—lest I should exalt myself beyond measure.
verses.12:8: Concerning this I appealed to the Lord three times that it might depart from me.
verses.12:9: And He has said to me, "My grace suffices for you, for power is brought to perfection in weakness." Most gladly therefore I shall rather boast in my weaknesses, so that the power of Christ may dwell upon me.
verses.12:10: Therefore I delight in weaknesses, in insults, in necessities, in persecutions and distresses, for Christ's sake; for whenever I am weak, then I am mighty.
verses.12:11: I have become a fool! You compelled me to it; for I ought to have been commended by you. Indeed, I was in no way inferior to these superlative apostles, even though I am nothing.
verses.12:12: Truly the signs of an apostle were accomplished among you with all perseverance, by signs and wonders and mighty works.
verses.12:13: For in what respect were you made inferior to the rest of the churches, except that I myself was not a burden to you? Forgive me this wrong!
verses.12:14: Behold, this third time I am ready to come to you, and I shall not be a burden; for I do not seek what is yours, but you. For children ought not to lay up treasure for their parents, but parents for their children.
verses.12:15: And I shall most gladly spend and be utterly spent for the sake of your souls. If I love you the more abundantly, am I to be loved the less?
verses.12:16: Be that as it may, I did not weigh you down; yet, being crafty, I caught you by deceit!
verses.12:17: Did I take advantage of you through any of those whom I have sent to you?
verses.12:18: I urged Titus to go, and sent the brother along with him. Did Titus take advantage of you? Did we not walk in the same spirit? Did we not walk in the very same footsteps?
verses.12:19: Have you been supposing all along that we are making our defense to you? It is before God in Christ that we speak; and all these things, beloved, are for your building up,
verses.12:20: for I fear lest somehow, when I come, I may find you not as I wish, and I myself may be found by you such as you do not wish—lest there be strife, jealousy, outbursts of wrath, selfish ambitions, slanders, whisperings, conceits, disorders;
verses.12:21: lest when I come again my God should humble me before you, and I should mourn over many of those who sinned formerly and have not repented of the impurity, sexual immorality, and licentiousness which they practiced.
verses.13:1: This third time I am coming to you. By the mouth of two or three witnesses every matter shall be established.
verses.13:2: I have forewarned, and I forewarn—as when present the second time and now while absent—those who have sinned previously and all the rest, that if I come again I will not spare,
verses.13:3: since you are seeking proof of Christ, who speaks in me. He is not weak toward you, but is powerful in you.
verses.13:4: For indeed He was crucified in weakness, yet He lives by the power of God. For we also are weak in Him, yet we shall live with Him by the power of God toward you.
verses.13:5: Test yourselves as to whether you are in the faith; prove yourselves. Or do you not recognize about yourselves that Jesus Christ is in you?—unless indeed you are unapproved.
verses.13:6: But I hope that you shall know that we ourselves are not unapproved.
verses.13:7: Now we pray to God that you may do no evil at all, not that we ourselves may appear approved, but that you may do what is noble, even though we may be as unapproved.
verses.13:8: For we have no power to do anything against the truth, but only for the truth.
verses.13:9: For we rejoice whenever we are weak, and you are strong; this also we pray for—your restoration.
verses.13:10: For this reason I write these things while absent, lest when present I should act severely, according to the authority which the Lord gave me, for building up and not for pulling down.
verses.13:11: Finally, brethren, rejoice, be restored, be encouraged, be of the same mind, be at peace; and the God of love and peace shall be with you.
verses.13:12: Greet one another with a holy kiss. All the saints send greetings to you.
verses.13:13: May the grace of the Lord Jesus Christ, and the love of God, and the communion of the Holy Spirit be with all of you.

notes.1:10: The critical text reads the future "will deliver" twice (Greek rhysetai), whereas later manuscripts read the present "does deliver" in the first clause.
notes.1:11: Greek ek pollon prosopon literally means "from many faces" (or "persons"), referring to the many believers whose intercessions obtain God's gracious deliverance for Paul.
notes.1:12: The earliest manuscripts read "holiness" (hagioteti), whereas later Byzantine manuscripts read "simplicity" (haploteti).
notes.1:20: The critical text reads "therefore also through Him is the 'Amen'" (dio kai di' autou to Amen), emphasizing Christ as the mediator through whom believers affirm God's promises.
notes.2:10: Greek en prosopo Christou literally means "in the face (or presence) of Christ," underscoring that Paul grants forgiveness under Christ's direct gaze and authority.
notes.2:14: Greek thriambeuo evokes a Roman triumphal procession in which a conqueror leads captives, portraying Paul as a conquered servant through whom the knowledge of Christ is spread abroad.
notes.2:17: The critical text reads "the many" (hoi polloi), contrasting Paul with numerous speakers who peddled religious teaching for financial gain (kapeleuontes).
notes.3:3: The critical text places "hearts" in dative apposition ("tablets that are hearts of flesh"), echoing the new-covenant promises of Jeremiah 31:33 and Ezekiel 11:19; 36:26.
notes.3:13: Greek telos can mean either "termination" (the fading end of the old glory) or "goal" (Christ as the ultimate aim of the Mosaic covenant).
notes.3:16: Echoing Exodus 34:34, the verb "turns" has no expressed subject in Greek, enabling Paul to extend Moses's turning to the Lord to anyone who turns to Him.
notes.3:18: Greek katoptrizomenoi can mean either "beholding as in a mirror" or "reflecting as in a mirror"; the closing phrase apo kyriou pneumatos literally reads "from the Lord, Spirit," linking back to 3:17.
notes.4:4: The critical Greek text omits "to them" after the verb, supporting the intransitive sense "lest the radiant light ... should shine forth" (or transitively, "lest they see the radiant light").
notes.4:14: Following the critical Greek text, which reads "Jesus" (without "the Lord") and "with Jesus" rather than "through Jesus."
notes.4:17: Literally "according to excess to excess," an emphatic Greek idiom conveying surpassing, incomparable measure.
notes.5:3: Following the critical Greek reading "once clothed" (endysamenoi); some manuscripts read "once unclothed" (ekdysamenoi).
notes.5:14: Following the critical Greek text, which omits "if" before "One died," presenting the statement directly rather than conditionally.
notes.5:17: The terse Greek phrase "kaine ktisis" has no expressed verb and may be rendered either "there is a new creation" or "he is a new creation." The critical Greek text also omits "all things" in the final clause, reading literally "behold, new things have come into being."
notes.5:21: Greek "hamartia" ("sin") here is often understood against the Septuagint background as bearing the sacrificial sense of a "sin offering," while Paul's wording concisely states "sin."
notes.6:12: Greek "splagchnois" literally refers to the inward parts, regarded in biblical idiom as the seat of deep affection and compassion.
notes.6:15: "Beliar" preserves the critical Greek form (Beliar), a variant of the Hebrew name Belial ("worthlessness"), used in Second Temple Jewish writings as a designation for Satan.
notes.6:16: Following the critical Greek text, which reads "we are the temple of the living God" rather than "you are."
notes.7:10: The Greek adjective ametamelēton ("without regret") may modify either "repentance" or "salvation"; in either case, sorrow according to God yields an enduring turning that brings no remorse.
notes.7:12: The critical Greek text reads "your earnestness on our behalf" (tēn spoudēn hymōn tēn hyper hēmōn), whereas later manuscripts invert the pronouns to "our earnestness for you."
notes.7:13: The critical text concludes the opening sentence at "we have been comforted" and begins the next with "besides our comfort," whereas later manuscripts attach "by your comfort" directly to the preceding clause.
notes.8:3: Paul's Greek in verses 3–4 is elliptical, omitting a finite verb ("they gave") as he rushes toward the Macedonians' self-giving in verse 5; later manuscripts insert "to receive" in verse 4 to smooth the construction.
notes.8:7: The critical text reads "the love from us that is in you" (tē ex hēmōn en hymin agapē), pointing to the love engendered in the Corinthians through Paul's ministry, whereas other manuscripts read "your love for us."
notes.8:19: The critical text reads "our own eagerness" (prothymian hēmōn), referring to Paul and his coworkers' willing readiness in administering the offering, while later manuscripts read "your eagerness."
notes.8:23: "Envoys" translates apostoloi (literally "apostles" or "sent ones"), used here for commissioned representatives of the churches rather than apostles of Christ in the strict office.
notes.9:5: "Blessing" (eulogia) here designates a generous, willing gift (cf. Gen 33:11), set in contrast to "covetousness" (pleonexia), which implies reluctant greed or a begrudged exaction.
notes.9:6: "With blessings" (ep' eulogiais) retains the lexical echo of "blessing" in verse 5, functioning idiomatically to mean bountifully or generously.
notes.9:9: Paul quotes Psalm 112:9 (LXX 111:9), where the pronouns refer to the generous righteous person who fears the Lord, though some readers also discern God's own liberality behind the words.
notes.9:10: The critical text employs future indicative verbs ("shall supply and multiply... and shall increase") as an assured promise, rather than the optative wish ("may He supply...") found in later manuscripts.
notes.10:4: The Greek dative τῷ θεῷ ('before God') may denote God's appraisal ('mighty in God's sight'), divine agency ('mighty through God'), or a Semitic-style superlative ('divinely mighty').
notes.10:7: The verb βλέπετε can be read as an imperative ('Look at what is before your face'), an indicative ('You look at outward appearances'), or an interrogative ('Do you look at outward appearances?').
notes.10:12: Some later manuscripts omit 'they are without understanding' (οὐ συνιᾶσιν) along with 'we' (ἡμεῖς) at the start of 10:13; the critical text retains both.
notes.11:3: The critical text includes 'and purity' (καὶ τῆς ἁγνότητος), echoing the 'pure virgin' imagery of 11:2; some later manuscripts omit this phrase.
notes.11:5: The ironic Greek phrase τῶν ὑπερλίαν ἀποστόλων (literally 'the super-extra apostles,' rendered 'these superlative apostles') is Paul's sarcastic designation for his rivals in Corinth (repeated in 12:11).
notes.11:23: The critical text follows the early manuscript order placing imprisonments before beatings ('in labors far more abundantly, in imprisonments far more often, in beatings beyond measure').
notes.12:7: Following the critical text punctuation, 'even by reason of the surpassing greatness of the revelations' completes the thought of 12:6, and Paul frames the thorn-in-the-flesh clause by repeating 'lest I should exalt myself beyond measure.'
notes.12:9: The critical text reads simply 'power' (ἡ γὰρ δύναμις) without 'My,' though Christ's power is clearly intended. The verb ἐπισκηνώσῃ literally means 'pitch a tent over' or 'tabernacle upon,' recalling God's dwelling presence.
notes.12:19: The critical text reads Πάλαι ('all along' or 'for a long time') rather than Πάλιν ('again'), which appears in later manuscripts.
notes.13:4: The Greek critical text reads simply 'For indeed He was crucified' without the conjunction 'though' found in some later manuscripts. The parallel prepositional phrases contrast the sphere of human weakness in Christ's crucifixion with the life-giving power of God in His resurrection.
notes.13:7: The critical text reads plural 'we pray' rather than singular 'I pray.' Across verses 5-7, Paul plays on a single Greek word family for testing and approval (dokimazo, dokimos, adokimos), rendered here as 'prove,' 'approved,' and 'unapproved.'
notes.13:11: The Greek imperative chairete can mean either 'rejoice' or 'farewell,' and Paul may intentionally evoke both senses in his closing words. The verb 'be restored' echoes 'restoration' in verse 9, signifying the mending and setting in order of the congregation.
notes.13:13: In the critical text, the greeting of all the saints belongs to verse 12, making this trinitarian benediction verse 13 rather than verse 14. The earliest manuscripts also end the letter here without a closing 'Amen.'
